courses.title: Applied Physics for Engineering I: Mechanics
outcomes: apply Newtonian mechanics and energy conservation to engineering problems
model vibrations and vibration control
analyze stress, strain, deformation, and material failure
courses.prerequisites: Engineering or physics foundations are recommended; course page targets engineering learners.

courses.title: Applied Physics for Engineering II: Thermofluids
outcomes: apply thermodynamics and fluid mechanics
analyze conduction, convection, and radiation
use thermofluid principles in HVAC, electronics cooling, aerodynamics, and energy systems
courses.prerequisites: Engineering or physics foundations are recommended.

courses.title: Applied Physics for Engineering III: Modern Physics
outcomes: understand Maxwell's equations and electromagnetic applications
connect optics, relativity, and quantum mechanics to technology
explain applications such as GPS, motors, photonics, and advanced materials
courses.prerequisites: Engineering or physics foundations are recommended.

courses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems I: Fundamentals of MEMS
outcomes: understand MEMS scaling laws and microscale physics
model beams, plates, and anchors
analyze electrostatic actuation, thermal effects, and silicon behavior
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets senior/graduate engineering learners and experienced technicians.

courses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems II: Design Principles
outcomes: build lumped-element models for MEMS
evaluate capacitive sensing, resonance, and Q-factor
analyze thermal stress, buckling, and fatigue in microsystems
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets senior/graduate engineering learners and experienced technicians; MEMS fundamentals are useful.

courses.title: Microelectromechanical Systems III: Fabrication Fundamentals
outcomes: compare bulk and surface micromachining
understand lithography, deposition, and etching effects
evaluate MEMS packaging, testing, and industrial constraints
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets senior/graduate engineering learners and experienced technicians; MEMS I/II are useful.

courses.title: Practical Mechanics For Inventors I: Mechanical Components
outcomes: select fasteners, bearings, springs, shafts, and couplings
evaluate gears, belts, chains, and linear motion
choose motors and actuators based on torque, speed, power, and precision
courses.prerequisites: Basic algebra and general familiarity with physics, forces, and motion are helpful; no prior machine-design experience required.

courses.title: Practical Mechanics For Inventors II: Designing Custom Parts
outcomes: translate requirements into mechanical designs
calculate stresses and evaluate failure modes
assess stiffness, deformation, vibration, mechanisms, and material tradeoffs
courses.prerequisites: Practical mechanical design foundations are useful; verify exact entry requirements on the course page.

courses.title: Industry 4.0 I: Foundations of Smart Manufacturing
outcomes: understand Industry 4.0 foundations
connect cyber-physical systems, IIoT, and digital twins
recognize OPC UA and MQTT communication standards
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets engineering/manufacturing learners; an engineering background is recommended.

courses.title: Industry 4.0 II: Advanced Manufacturing Technologies
outcomes: compare additive manufacturing technologies
understand smart materials and advanced CNC
integrate cobots and autonomous mobile robots into workflows
courses.prerequisites: Industry 4.0 foundations are useful; verify exact prerequisites on the course page.

courses.title: Industry 4.0 III: Advanced Computational Technologies
outcomes: understand supervised and unsupervised machine learning
apply ML concepts to fault detection and predictive maintenance
understand computer vision for industrial inspection
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets engineering learners and technicians; check current page for exact requirements.

courses.title: Plastics Engineering I: Intro To Polymers
outcomes: understand polymer science and structure
compare mechanical and thermal properties
use testing methods and material-selection reasoning
courses.prerequisites: Course page targets engineering/material science learners and manufacturing professionals.

courses.title: Plastics Engineering II: Plastic Injection & Mold Design
outcomes: understand injection molding and mold components
reason about gates, runners, cooling, and process variables
troubleshoot common molding defects and design for manufacturability
courses.prerequisites: Plastics Engineering I is optional according to the public course page.

courses.title: Plastics Engineering III: Industrial Polymer Processing
outcomes: understand extrusion, thermoforming, blow molding, and rotational molding
evaluate additives and fiber reinforcements
explore polymer recycling and industrial applications
courses.prerequisites: Plastics Engineering I and II are optional according to the public course page.
